atoms.text: This guide describes how to configure the S3 bucket example-flow-logs to receive network flow logs from FlowTrace, a fictional traffic-recording service. FlowTrace writes compressed log objects every 10 minutes under the prefix flowtrace/AWSLogs/ followed by the sending account ID. Before enabling delivery, attach a bucket policy statement with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:PutObject. Set the Principal to the AWS account ID of the FlowTrace delivery account for your Region, written as arn:aws:iam::198765432109:root. Set Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-flow-logs/flowtrace/AWSLogs/* so the grant covers only the delivery prefix. Add a Condition using StringEquals on s3:x-amz-acl with the value bucket-owner-full-control, so the bucket owner owns every delivered object. Add a second statement that allows s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket ARN for the same account principal, because FlowTrace checks bucket ownership before its first write. Do not grant list, read, or delete permissions to this principal. After saving the policy, enable the flow log in the FlowTrace console, select the bucket as the destination, and confirm that the first objects appear within 15 minutes.

This guide describes how to configure the S3 bucket example-flow-logs to receive network flow logs from FlowTrace, a fictional traffic-recording service. FlowTrace writes compressed log objects every 10 minutes under the prefix flowtrace/AWSLogs/ followed by the sending account ID. Before enabling delivery, attach a bucket policy statement with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:PutObject. Set the Principal to the service principal flowtrace.amazonaws.com, written as a Service element rather than an AWS element. Set Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-flow-logs/flowtrace/AWSLogs/* so the grant covers only the delivery prefix. Add Condition entries using StringEquals on s3:x-amz-acl with the value bucket-owner-full-control and on aws:SourceAccount with your own account ID, so only flow logs from your account are accepted and the bucket owner owns every object. Add a second statement that allows s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket ARN for the same service principal, with the same aws:SourceAccount condition, because FlowTrace checks bucket ownership before its first write. Do not grant list, read, or delete permissions to this principal. After saving the policy, enable the flow log in the FlowTrace console, select the bucket as the destination, and confirm that the first objects appear within 15 minutes.

This section covers delivery of load balancer access logs from BalanceScope, a fictional traffic-distribution service, to the S3 bucket example-lb-access-logs. BalanceScope writes one log object per node every five minutes under the prefix lb-logs/. The bucket must be in the same Region as the load balancer. Add a bucket policy statement with Effect Allow and Action s3:PutObject. Name the Principal as the IAM role arn:aws:iam::203948576102:role/balancescope-log-writer, which the delivery workflow uses to write objects. Scope Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-lb-access-logs/lb-logs/* so that writes outside that prefix are denied by default. Add a Condition using ArnLike on aws:PrincipalArn is not needed here; instead rely on the role named in the Principal element and keep the statement limited to a single action. Do not allow s3:DeleteObject for this role, so that delivered logs cannot be removed through this path. Then enable access logging on the load balancer, specify the bucket name and the lb-logs prefix, and verify a test object after the next five-minute interval.

This section covers delivery of load balancer access logs from BalanceScope, a fictional traffic-distribution service, to the S3 bucket example-lb-access-logs. BalanceScope writes one log object per node every five minutes under the prefix lb-logs/. The bucket must be in the same Region as the load balancer. Add a bucket policy statement with Effect Allow and Action s3:PutObject. Name the Principal as the service principal logs.balancescope.amazonaws.com, which the delivery workflow uses to write objects. Scope Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-lb-access-logs/lb-logs/* so that writes outside that prefix are denied by default. Add a Condition using ArnLike on aws:SourceArn with the value of your load balancer ARN pattern and StringEquals on aws:SourceAccount, which prevents other customers' resources from using the service to write here. Do not allow s3:DeleteObject for this principal, so that delivered logs cannot be removed through this path. Then enable access logging on the load balancer, specify the bucket name and the lb-logs prefix, and verify a test object after the next five-minute interval.

This procedure sets up the S3 bucket example-edge-logs to store request logs from EdgeRelay, a fictional content-distribution service. EdgeRelay batches log lines into gzip objects and writes them hourly under the prefix edge/requests/. Create a bucket policy statement with Effect Allow and the actions s3:PutObject and s3:GetBucketAcl. Set the Principal to the AWS account ID arn:aws:iam::305811220946:root, which is the account EdgeRelay uses to write to customer buckets. Set Resource to both the bucket ARN and arn:aws:s3:::example-edge-logs/edge/requests/*, using separate statements if you prefer to separate bucket-level and object-level permissions. Add a Condition that requires s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control for object writes. Turn off ACL-based public access on the bucket so that the policy is the only grant in effect. In the EdgeRelay console, open the distribution settings, enable standard logging, and enter the bucket name and the prefix. The first hourly object should appear within about 60 minutes, and you can check it with an s3 listing of the prefix.

This procedure sets up the S3 bucket example-edge-logs to store request logs from EdgeRelay, a fictional content-distribution service. EdgeRelay batches log lines into gzip objects and writes them hourly under the prefix edge/requests/. Create a bucket policy statement with Effect Allow and the actions s3:PutObject and s3:GetBucketAcl. Set the Principal to the service principal edgerelay.amazonaws.com, which is the identity EdgeRelay uses to write to customer buckets. Set Resource to both the bucket ARN and arn:aws:s3:::example-edge-logs/edge/requests/*, using separate statements if you prefer to separate bucket-level and object-level permissions. Add a Condition that requires s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control for object writes, and add aws:SourceArn matching your distribution ARN. Turn off ACL-based public access on the bucket so that the policy is the only grant in effect. In the EdgeRelay console, open the distribution settings, enable standard logging, and enter the bucket name and the prefix. The first hourly object should appear within about 60 minutes, and you can check it with an s3 listing of the prefix.

This guide explains how to receive API request logs from GatewayLens, a fictional API management service, in the S3 bucket example-api-logs. GatewayLens writes JSON-formatted objects partitioned by date under the prefix api/yyyy/mm/dd/. The writes are performed by an IAM user, arn:aws:iam::412233445566:user/gatewaylens-logger, which is created in a dedicated delivery account. Add a bucket policy statement that allows s3:PutObject for that IAM user on arn:aws:s3:::example-api-logs/api/*. Add a Condition using StringEquals on s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption with the value AES256, so that only encrypted objects are accepted. Add a Deny statement for s3:PutObject when aws:SecureTransport is false, which forces TLS for every write. Keep the bucket policy free of read actions, because log consumers use a separate analytics role. Enable log delivery in the GatewayLens stage settings and choose the bucket and prefix. Validate the configuration by sending a test request and checking for the partitioned object within ten minutes.

This guide explains how to receive API request logs from GatewayLens, a fictional API management service, in the S3 bucket example-api-logs. GatewayLens writes JSON-formatted objects partitioned by date under the prefix api/yyyy/mm/dd/. The writes are performed by the service principal gatewaylens.amazonaws.com, which acts on behalf of APIs in your own account. Add a bucket policy statement that allows s3:PutObject for that service principal on arn:aws:s3:::example-api-logs/api/*. Add a Condition using StringEquals on s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption with the value AES256, so that only encrypted objects are accepted, and StringEquals on aws:SourceAccount with your account ID. Add a Deny statement for s3:PutObject when aws:SecureTransport is false, which forces TLS for every write. Keep the bucket policy free of read actions, because log consumers use a separate analytics role. Enable log delivery in the GatewayLens stage settings and choose the bucket and prefix. Validate the configuration by sending a test request and checking for the partitioned object within ten minutes.

This section configures the S3 bucket example-audit-trail to hold management event records from TrailKeeper, a fictional account auditing service. TrailKeeper writes a digest file and event files per Region under the prefix trail/AWSLogs/ followed by the account ID. First, add a statement that allows s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket ARN. Set the Principal to arn:aws:iam::520019384756:root, the AWS account identifier published for TrailKeeper in your Region. Second, add a statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-trail/trail/AWSLogs/111122223333/*, where 111122223333 is your account ID. Use the same account principal and require s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control. Do not use wildcards for the account ID segment unless you are collecting trails from several accounts. After saving the policy, create the trail in the TrailKeeper console and select the bucket. If the policy is incomplete, trail creation fails with an insufficient permissions error that names the missing action.

This section configures the S3 bucket example-audit-trail to hold management event records from TrailKeeper, a fictional account auditing service. TrailKeeper writes a digest file and event files per Region under the prefix trail/AWSLogs/ followed by the account ID. First, add a statement that allows s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket ARN. Set the Principal to the service principal trailkeeper.amazonaws.com, and add aws:SourceArn matching your trail ARN. Second, add a statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-trail/trail/AWSLogs/111122223333/*, where 111122223333 is your account ID. Use the same service principal and require s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control. Do not use wildcards for the account ID segment unless you are collecting trails from several accounts. After saving the policy, create the trail in the TrailKeeper console and select the bucket. If the policy is incomplete, trail creation fails with an insufficient permissions error that names the missing action.

This procedure prepares the S3 bucket example-dns-query-logs for DNS query logging from ResolverLog, a fictional name-resolution service. ResolverLog writes one object per five-minute window under the prefix dns/queries/, each containing newline-delimited query records. Add a bucket policy statement with Effect Allow and Action s3:PutObject. Set the Principal to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::637482910563:role/resolverlog-delivery, which ResolverLog's delivery component assumes when writing. Limit Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-dns-query-logs/dns/queries/*. Adda second statement allowing s3:GetBucketLocation for the same role, since the writer resolves the bucket Region before delivery. Add a lifecycle rule to expire objects under dns/queries/ after 90 days, which is independent of the access policy. Open the ResolverLog configuration for the hosted zone and create a query logging configuration that points to the bucket. Verify that objects arrive after the first window and that their size is nonzero.

This procedure prepares the S3 bucket example-dns-query-logs for DNS query logging from ResolverLog, a fictional name-resolution service. ResolverLog writes one object per five-minute window under the prefix dns/queries/, each containing newline-delimited query records. Add a bucket policy statement with Effect Allow and Action s3:PutObject. Set the Principal to the service principal delivery.resolverlog.amazonaws.com, which ResolverLog uses directly when writing. Limit Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-dns-query-logs/dns/queries/*, and add aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn conditions for your hosted zone. Add a second statement allowing s3:GetBucketLocation for the same service principal, since the writer resolves the bucket Region before delivery. Add a lifecycle rule to expire objects under dns/queries/ after 90 days, which is independent of the access policy. Open the ResolverLog configuration for the hosted zone and create a query logging configuration that points to the bucket. Verify that objects arrive after the first window and that their size is nonzero.

This guide describes a central log archive bucket, example-central-logs, that receives logs from FlowTrace in three member accounts: 111111111111, 222222222222, and 333333333333. Each account delivers to its own prefix, such as archive/111111111111/. Create one statement per account so permissions can be revoked independently. In each statement, set Effect to Allow and Action to s3:PutObject, and name the Principal as the delivery role in that account, for example arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/flowtrace-delivery. Set Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-central-logs/archive/111111111111/*, changing the account ID per statement. Add a Condition requiring s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control in every statement. Create the bucket in a dedicated security account and enable versioning to retain prior object versions. In each member account, enable FlowTrace delivery to the bucket with the matching prefix. Verify delivery per account by listing each prefix after the first interval.

This guide describes a central log archive bucket, example-central-logs, that receives logs from FlowTrace in three member accounts: 111111111111, 222222222222, and 333333333333. Each account delivers to its own prefix, such as archive/111111111111/. Create one statement per account so permissions can be revoked independently. In each statement, set Effect to Allow and Action to s3:PutObject, and name the Principal as the service principal flowtrace.amazonaws.com. Set Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-central-logs/archive/111111111111/*, changing the account ID per statement, and add a matching aws:SourceAccount condition with that same account ID. Add a Condition requiring s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control in every statement. Create the bucket in a dedicated security account and enable versioning to retain prior object versions. In each member account, enable FlowTrace delivery to the bucket with the matching prefix. Verify delivery per account by listing each prefix after the first interval.

This section covers audit log export from VaultDB, a fictional managed database service, to the S3 bucket example-db-audit. VaultDB exports audit records as Parquet files under the prefix vaultdb/audit/ once every 15 minutes. Add a bucket policy statement with Effect Allow and the actions s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload, since large exports use multipart uploads. Set the Principal to the AWS account ID arn:aws:iam::748201936475:root, which is the export account used by VaultDB. Limit Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-db-audit/vaultdb/audit/*. Add a Condition using StringEquals on s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption with the value aws:kms, and on s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id with your key ARN. Grant the same principal permission to use the key in the key policy, which is configured separately. Enable audit export on the database cluster and specify the bucket and prefix. Confirm that Parquet files appear after the first interval and that they report the expected encryption key.

Add a Condition using StringEquals on s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption with the value aws:kms, and on s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id with your key ARN.
